title: Exact quantum fanout in constant depth with unrestricted circuit size
formal: Does there exist a fixed integer d such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), some finite QAC circuit of depth at most d exactly implements FANOUT\(_{n}\) on one control qubit and n target qubits, allowing arbitrarily many clean ancillas and no size bound?
why: Determines whether unbounded-arity quantum AND operations and one-qubit gates can express coherent fanout in bounded depth at any finite size. It isolates a basic limitation of shallow unitary computation that cannot be explained solely by insufficient circuit width.
status_note: Exact implementation definition, gate set and arbitrary-size footnote checked, with later August 2026 abstracts searched through 11 September 2026. No matching exact constant-depth construction or all-size impossibility result was located.

progress.text: The ITCS paper explicitly records arbitrary-size exact fanout as open and distinguishes it from approximate constructions.
The revised Fourier-concentration preprint still describes the related parity question as open while proving additional equivalences.

importance.reason: Isolates a basic exact-unitary expressiveness question in constant-depth quantum computation even when finite size and ancilla count are unrestricted. The existing numerical score is retained during formulation review.

sentences: Quantum fanout coherently flips every target qubit according to one control qubit.
The problem asks whether one constant depth bound can implement it exactly using arbitrary one-qubit and generalized Toffoli gates.
The circuit may have any finite size and any finite number of clean ancillas.
Superposition inputs must be handled correctly and the ancillas must return to zero.
An exact construction or an impossibility theorem would determine whether this basic operation lies beyond the expressive power of the shallow gate model.

definitions: For bits \(s,x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}\in \{0,1\}\), FANOUT\(_{n}|s,x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}\rangle =|s,s\oplus x_{1},\ldots ,s\oplus x_{n}\rangle\), extended linearly to all states; ⊕ is addition modulo two. A permitted circuit acts on \(n+1+a(n)\) qubits for some finite \(a(n)\ge 0\). Its gates are arbitrary one-qubit unitary matrices over \(\mathbb{C}\) and generalized Toffoli gates: for any \(k\ge 1\) distinct controls and a distinct target, |\(z_{1},\ldots ,z_{k},t\rangle\) maps to |\(z_{1},\ldots ,z_{k},t\oplus (z_{1}\cdots z_{k})\rangle\). Each layer contains gates on disjoint sets of qubits, and depth is the number of layers. Gates may connect any qubits; fanout gates, measurements, postselection and classical feed-forward are not additional primitives. Exact implementation means that for some global phase \(e^{i\varphi _{n}}\), independent of the input state \(\psi , C_{n}(|\psi \rangle \otimes |0\rangle ^{\otimes}a(n))=e^{i\varphi _{n}}\)(FANOUT\(_{n}|\psi \rangle\))⊗|\(0\rangle ^{\otimes}a(n)\) for every unit vector \(\psi\) in \((\mathbb{C} ^{2})^{\otimes}(n+1)\). The ancillas must return to zero, as in the source’s implementation definition. Gate count, ancilla count and gate arities may grow arbitrarily with n but must be finite at each n. The family is nonuniform: there is no required circuit-generation algorithm or finite gate alphabet. The one depth bound d must work for all n. QAC0 usually adds a polynomial-size bound; this question explicitly drops it.
answer_criterion: Construct an exact clean-ancilla implementation with a depth bound independent of n, or prove that no such bound exists even when size, ancilla count and Toffoli arity are unrestricted. An approximation with arbitrarily small nonzero error, a lower bound only for polynomial-size circuits, or a bound for one fixed small depth does not settle this formulation.

context_blocks.title: Fanout is a coherent controlled operation
context_blocks.text: On a basis input, the control flips every target when it is one and leaves them unchanged when it is zero. The same circuit must act correctly on superpositions, including inputs entangled with other systems. Agreement only on measured classical outputs would be weaker.

context_blocks.title: This operation does not clone an arbitrary quantum state
context_blocks.text: For example, applying two-target fanout to |+⟩|\(00\rangle\) yields \((|000\rangle +|111\rangle )/\sqrt{2}\). It does not yield three independent copies of |+⟩. The target is therefore compatible with the distinction between coherent basis fanout and cloning.

context_blocks.title: Only depth is restricted
context_blocks.text: A Toffoli gate may inspect many controls in one layer, but a qubit cannot participate in several gates in that same layer. The question permits enormous circuits and arbitrarily many zero-initialized ancillas. A negative answer would therefore be a structural limitation of constant depth, beyond ordinary polynomial-size lower bounds.

context_blocks.title: Exactness remains separate from approximation
context_blocks.text: The ITCS paper discusses approximate implementations and records exact fanout as open even without a size bound. Its known parity/fanout equivalence and later 2026 equivalence results connect the task to other shallow quantum operations, but do not constitute the exact implementation or impossibility theorem requested here.
